title: A rising early-warning score that has not reached the call-out level
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Original practical exercise with fictional people; never imported, published or shown to learners.
gaps: No published exercise may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The wording, answers and explanations are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical or educational review.
The exercise has not been tested with learners, and its Arabic version has not been written.
NEWS2 is a UK tool and ICU units may use other tools and continuous monitoring.
No numeric thresholds are written; they come from the local policy and the official chart.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register for each source's reproduction status.
objectives: Treat an early-warning score as an aid to judgement and act on a worsening trend.

sources.use: NEWS2 report: aid to clinical judgement, record the oxygen device, escalation by policy

required_sources: The unit's early-warning and escalation policy
A source on trend-based escalation in critical care
setup: A fictional adult on a fictional ward; three sets of observations over six hours show a rising score, none at the call-out level.

options.text: Use clinical judgement: share the trend and your concern with the responsible clinician according to the unit's policy, and repeat observations as the policy directs.
options.feedback: Early-warning scores aid, and do not replace, clinical assessment; a worsening trend deserves escalation. If severe deterioration or immediate danger is apparent, activate the local emergency response without waiting for a score threshold or scheduled repeat observations.

options.text: Wait until the score reaches the call-out level because the policy has not been triggered.
options.feedback: Waiting for a trigger can lose valuable time when the trend is clearly worsening.

options.text: Change the score by re-measuring until the number looks better.
options.feedback: Observations are recorded as measured; manipulating them hides deterioration.

options.text: Ignore the trend because each single score looks acceptable.
options.feedback: A series of acceptable-looking scores can hide a steady decline.
